name: Mistral Large 4 (1T-A52B)

lineage.how_derived: trained from scratch on 3,800 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs in Mistral's own European datacentres (card); the smaller family members in this database are mistral-small-4-119b-a6b and mistral-medium-3.5-128b

purpose: The card calls it Mistral's largest and most capable model: one set of weights unifying instruction following, reasoning, coding and agentic work, strong in cybersecurity, finance and law, with state-of-the-art visual grounding among open weights and fluency in 160+ languages including every official EU language.

license.name: Mistral Ecosystem Open-Weight License (modified MIT)
license.notes: LICENSE text read (2.6 KB). MIT-style grant including weights, derivatives and sale. One condition: whoever operates a Model-as-a-Service business must obtain a separate commercial licence from Mistral before using the model or derivatives for any commercial purpose (MaaS means giving third parties inference or post-training access with meaningful control over inputs, parameters or training data). End-user products that embed the model in specific features, mere request relaying, internal use and use via Mistral's official products are not affected. No revenue threshold, no territory exclusion.

architecture.kind: multimodal sparse MoE with MLA and an indexer (sparse attention), vision encoder, DSpark draft head
architecture.attention: MLA (kv_lora_rank 512, 64 heads, hidden 6144) with an indexer (32 index heads, top-k 2048) and shared indexer layers; NoPE layers every 4th; final logit soft-capping 30
architecture.drafter: DSpark: 3 dense MLA draft layers in BF16 proposing blocks of 3 tokens, shipped inside the checkpoint; up to 1.9x throughput (vendor); standalone DSpark GGUFs of 2.25 to 4.21 GB exist
architecture.why_this_design: The card names the choices (granular MoE with 128 routed experts, 4 active and 1 shared; 1M context; Pixtral-style variable-size vision encoder) but gives no reasons for the numbers. 49B active (52B including embeddings and output layers).

variants.format: safetensors FP8 block-quantised (config fp8, weight block 128x128)

variants.notes: vendor says smaller footprint and same performance; size not measured
Q2_K 380.71, Q4_K_M 634.8, Q8_0 1115.15 GB; linked by the vendor card for llama.cpp
also MLX 2-bit and 4-bit text-only repos (mlx-community) and an MLX Q3i repo; sizes not measured

pc-12gb.notes: smallest GGUF 233 GB against about 60 GB

pc-32gb.notes: UD-IQ1_S 233 GB against about 158 GB (29.6 VRAM + 128 RAM)

mac-64gb+.notes: 233 GB against about 52 GB GPU share on a 64 GB Mac; Macs with 256 GB or more not assessed

engine_support.notes: The vendor card links the ggml-org GGUFs for llama.cpp and an Unsloth guide.

benchmarks.name: Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index
benchmarks.variant: full model; effectively tied with GLM-5.3 (47 % fewer tokens per task), as quoted on the vendor card from Artificial Analysis

benchmarks.name: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5
benchmarks.variant: full model; highest among western open-weight models, below the leading Chinese open models (card)

strengths: Cybersecurity, finance, law and visual grounding (vendor)
Fewer tokens per coding task than the leading open model (47 % fewer, Artificial Analysis via vendor card)
weaknesses: Behind the leading Chinese open models on the aggregate index (card says so)
soft.behavior: Reasoning effort low, medium or high (default high); recommended temperature 1.0 and top_p 0.95; keep the tool set small (card).
soft.maturity: Mistral is an established European lab; about 26 derivatives on the HF API within seven weeks.

tona_fit.reason: A 1T-parameter model with 49B active; the smallest public quant (233 GB) exceeds even the 32 GB VRAM + 128 GB RAM class. Its independent Coding Agent Index (48 %) does not beat the far smaller DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on the vendor numbers we have. The relevant Mistral models for our users are the Small 4 and Medium 3.5 records.
